content:
Data handling teaches Class 2 children to read pictographs, tally marks and tables — careful-counting Olympiad questions. Here is what the Maths Olympiad Class 2 data handling chapter tests, the facts, the slips, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 2 Maths Olympiad Data Handling chapter tests

  • Reading a pictograph and its key (a symbol may equal 2, 5 or 10)
  • Tally marks
  • Simple tables
  • Interpreting data — most, fewest, how many more, totals

Key facts your child should know

  • In a pictograph, multiply the pictures by the key to get the count.
  • A tally counts in groups of five — the fifth mark crosses the first four.
  • Most = the biggest number; fewest = the smallest.
  • "How many more" is a subtraction; the total is the sum of every row.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Ignoring the key and counting each symbol as 1.
  • Adding rows when the question asks how many more.
  • Miscounting tally groups of five.

quiz.title: IMO Class 2 Data Handling Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: IMO Maths Olympiad Class 2: Data Handling

questions.q: Umesh counted birds on a wire using tally marks. The count shows 2 bundles of five and 4 single marks. What is the number counted?
questions.explanation: Each bundle is 5. So 2 bundles make 10, and 4 more singles give 10 + 4 = 14.

questions.q: The table shows plants in gardens: Front 17, Back 21, Side 13, Terrace 15. What is the total shown by the whole table?
The table shows pets in a colony: Dogs 17, Cats 23, Rabbits 12, Parrots 20. Which pet is seen the most in the colony?
questions.explanation: Compare the numbers: 17, 23, 12, 20. The biggest is 23, which belongs to Cats.

questions.q: In a tally chart, white sheep are shown by 3 bundles of five and 2 singles, while black sheep are shown by 1 bundles of five and 4 singles. How many more are the white sheep than the black sheep?
In a pictograph, 1 symbol stands for 5 beads. Omkar's row has 9 symbols. How many beads is that?
questions.explanation: Each symbol means 5 beads. Count in fives: 9 × 5 = 45 beads.

questions.q: In a pictograph, 1 symbol stands for 1 feather. Isha's row shows 12 symbols and Om's row shows 7 symbols. How many feathers do the two rows show altogether?
questions.explanation: Each symbol is 1 feather. Add the two rows: 12 + 7 = 19 feathers.

questions.q: In a pictograph, 1 symbol stands for 2 balloons. Kunal's row has 10 symbols. How many balloons does Kunal's row show?
questions.explanation: Each symbol means 2 balloons. So 10 symbols show 10 × 2 = 20 balloons.

questions.q: Tanu counted cars passing the school gate using tally marks. The count shows 5 bundles of five and 1 single marks. What is the number counted?
questions.explanation: Each bundle is 5. So 5 bundles make 25, and 1 more singles give 25 + 1 = 26.

questions.q: The table shows fish in tanks: Tank A 13, Tank B 22, Tank C 16, Tank D 12. What is the total shown by the whole table?
A table shows trading cards with four children: Trading cards owned — Qamar 30, Rishi 24, Sonu 35, Tanya 19. Who has the second highest number of trading cards?
questions.explanation: From most to least: Sonu (35), Qamar (30), Rishi (24), Tanya (19). The second highest is Qamar.

faq.a: It tells you how many each picture stands for — one symbol might mean 2, 5 or 10 items, so you multiply to get the real count.

faq.q: How do you read tally marks?
faq.a: Count in fives: every fifth mark crosses the previous four, so groups of five are quick to add.
